To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have integrated optical microscopy into the high-speed atomic-force microscopy (AFM) path, allowing high-speed AFM imaging on cells, and have used it to visualize single aquaporin-4 proteins on intact eye lens cells.

we have developed a new hybrid high-speed atomic for microscopy/optical microscopy technique, that we have used it to study the membrane of intact cells, and that it allows us to image membrane protein dynamics in the plasma membranes of intact eye lens epithelial cells at 960 frames per second.
we have developed a novel hybrid microscope for high-speed imaging of single membrane proteins on cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hybrid high-speed atomic-force microscopy/optical microscopy system for the study of single membrane proteins on intact eukaryotic (eye) lens cells.

the development and implementation of novel methods for the analysis of the structure and function of biological macromolecules, and in the application of these methods to the study of biological problems.
the development of a hybrid high-speed atomic microscopy/optical microscopy system for the visualization of membrane proteins in living eukaryotic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid high-speed atomic-force optical microscope allows for the first time the direct observation of single membrane proteins in the plasma membrane in a living cell.
the presented hybrid high-speed atomic-force microscopy/optical microscopy technique allows imaging of unlabelled single membrane proteins on living cells with a time resolution in the range of 1 s.
this hybrid microscope enables a new era of single molecule imaging of proteins in their natural environment, which will provide new insights into the function and dynamics of proteins in the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a high-speed atomic force microscope that allows us to study single membrane proteins on intact eukaryotic live cells.

we have developed a high-speed AFM/OM hybrid system, which allows high-speed AFM imaging of single membrane proteins on intact cells, and that the system is able to image membrane protein dynamics on a eukaroytic cell.
we have developed a high-speed atomic force microscope that is capable of imaging biological samples in their native state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of high-speed atomic for microscopy with optical microscopy allows the study of single membrane proteins in their native cellular environment.
high-speed atomic force microscope is now able to visualize single molecules on a eukayotic cell under physiological condition.
the combination of optical microscopy and high-speed atomic force microscopes can be used for the visualization of single molecules on living cells.
